2609.17226.title: Easy to Catch a Liar, Hard to Clear an Honest One: Language Models Diagnosing a Corrupted Reward Channel from a Verified Record
2609.17226.paper_summary: An agent that learns from rewards has to trust whatever reports those rewards. When the reports suddenly change, either the world changed or the reporter broke. From the reports alone these are indistinguishable, and reinforcement learning theory shows that no amount of further experience separates them. The prescribed escape is richer data about the reporter itself. We ask whether a frozen language model, handed exactly that data, uses it. We build a two-option game in which a payout swap and a lying reporter produce byte-identical histories. Then we add one verified record: an independent check of one round's real result, printed beside what the reporter said about that round. That single line settles the case. We ask three large models, from two families, to answer one question with one letter. Is the reporter honest or lying? They catch a lying reporter almost perfectly. At the 70B class that holds in every condition we tried; the 32B model slips in one wording. They clear an honest reporter far less often, and how often depends on things that should not matter. Averaged over rounds, letters, and wordings, a 72B model calls an honest reporter a liar 38% of the time when nothing has changed at all, and 58% of the time when the payouts moved. A 70B model from a second family calls an honest reporter a liar 26% and 48% of the time. The failure is not one of reading, because in the situation where nothing changed the same models score 0.96 to 1.00 with the answer printed in the prompt. Which surface feature drives it differs by family. For the Qwen models it is which round the record names, and for Llama it is which letter stands for "honest." Adding the record to a prompt that already states the answer makes Llama less likely to give that answer. We had registered a prediction for that 58% before the run: 35%. The failure is larger than we expected.
2609.17226.paper_summary_zh: 一個從獎勵中學習的代理必須信任那些報告獎勵的內容。當報告突然改變時，要麼是世界發生了變化，要麼是報告者出錯。僅從報告中無法區分這兩者，而強化學習理論顯示，無論進一步的經驗有多少，都無法將它們分開。建議的解決方案是獲取有關報告者本身的更豐富數據。我們詢問一個凍結的語言模型，是否會利用這些數據。我們構建了一個雙選擇遊戲，其中一個支付交換和一個說謊的報告者產生了字節相同的歷史記錄。然後我們添加了一個經過驗證的記錄：對一輪真實結果的獨立檢查，並將其打印在報告者對該輪的說法旁邊。這一行解決了問題。我們要求來自兩個家族的三個大型模型用一個字母回答一個問題。報告者是誠實的還是說謊的？他們幾乎完美地抓住了說謊的報告者。在我們嘗試的每一種條件下，70B級別的模型都保持一致；32B模型在一種措辭上出錯。他們對誠實報告者的判斷遠不如對說謊者的判斷準確，而這種準確性取決於一些不應該影響的因素。平均來看，在回合、字母和措辭中，72B模型在什麼都沒有改變的情況下，將誠實報告者稱為說謊者的比例為38%，而在支付變動的情況下則為58%。來自第二個家族的70B模型將誠實報告者稱為說謊者的比例為26%和48%。這種失敗並不是閱讀的問題，因為在沒有變化的情況下，同樣的模型在答案打印在提示中的情況下得分為0.96到1.00。驅動這種現象的表面特徵因家族而異。對於Qwen模型而言，關鍵在於記錄命名的回合，而對於Llama而言，則是代表“誠實”的字母。將記錄添加到已經表明答案的提示中會使Llama不太可能給出該答案。在運行之前，我們對那58%的預測為35%。這一失敗比我們預期的要大。
2609.17226.author: Arman Nik Khah et.al.
